title: Thirty-, sixty-, and ninety-day study plans
objectives: Build a 30/60/90-day Salesforce study plan around a target role, official credential pages, and Trailhead—not around dumps.
Map days 1–30 to foundations, 31–60 to role-typed mocks and a credential slice, 61–90 to integration of stories, whiteboards, and a measured exam or interview date.
Use Trailhead career planning (discover/plan/act, learning/earning/connecting) as the official planning spine.
Put calendar blocks, a mock type, and an official URL on each phase—not a vague 'study Salesforce.'
diagnostic_question: You want a Platform Administrator job in 90 days. What belongs in the first thirty days versus sixty versus ninety, and which unofficial PDF does not belong at all?
definition: Thirty-, sixty-, and ninety-day study plans are calendarized skill plans toward a Salesforce role or credential. Trailhead Career Development Planning tells you to discover, plan, and act; to skill up via learning, earning credentials, and connecting; and to block weekly time. Official credential pages and career paths (Admin, Developer, Architect) plus Get Job Ready are the syllabus. Dumps are not. ([Create a plan](https://trailhead.salesforce.com/content/learn/modules/career-development-planning/create-a-plan-and-skill-up); [Assess yourself](https://trailhead.salesforce.com/content/learn/modules/career-development-planning/assess-yourself); [Get Job Ready](https://trailhead.salesforce.com/content/learn/trails/get-job-ready))
why_it_matters: Unplanned study becomes badge collecting or dump memorization. Interviewers and hiring managers also ask what you will do in your first 90 days on the job—the same discipline applies to study: sequenced outcomes, not vibes.
sixty_second_explanation: Treat 30/60/90 like a training-camp calendar. Days 1–30 are foundations and conditioning: Admin or Developer career-path trails, one playground habit, a resume audit. Days 31–60 are scrimmages: role-typed mocks, which-tool, debug protocol, one official cert-prep slice. Days 61–90 are game weeks: full mocks, story bank, exam or interview date, connecting in Trailblazer Community. A dump PDF is not a playbook.
deeper_explanation: Assess Yourself: career planning is ongoing; discover, plan, act. A 90-day plan is one act cycle, not a lifetime contract. ([Assess yourself](https://trailhead.salesforce.com/content/learn/modules/career-development-planning/assess-yourself))

Create a Plan and Skill Up: learning (Trailhead), earning (badges/certs), connecting (community). Block weekly time; review the plan. V2MOM-like worksheets are optional structure. ([Create a plan](https://trailhead.salesforce.com/content/learn/modules/career-development-planning/create-a-plan-and-skill-up))

Get Job Ready packages career planning, resume, and interview strategies—the 60–90 day job-hunt overlay. ([Get Job Ready](https://trailhead.salesforce.com/content/learn/trails/get-job-ready); [Interview Strategies](https://trailhead.salesforce.com/content/learn/modules/interview-strategies); [Resume strategies](https://trailhead.salesforce.com/content/learn/modules/resume-strategies))

Admin, Developer, and Architect career paths plus credential pages are the official syllabi. Beginner admin trail remains a 30-day foundation option. ([Admin path](https://trailhead.salesforce.com/career-path/admin); [Developer path](https://trailhead.salesforce.com/career-path/developer); [Architect path](https://trailhead.salesforce.com/career-path/architect); [Admin beginner trail](https://trailhead.salesforce.com/content/learn/trails/force_com_admin_beginner); [Platform Administrator](https://trailhead.salesforce.com/en/credentials/platformadministrator); [Prepare for development opportunities](https://trailhead.salesforce.com/content/learn/trails/prepare-for-development-opportunities-in-the-salesforce-ecosystem))
Do not copy unofficial exam weights from blogs. Reverify live credential pages. Do not schedule dumps.

mental_model.analogy: Training-camp calendar: conditioning (30), scrimmages (60), game weeks (90)—official playbooks only, no stolen opponent sheets.
useful_mapping: 30 days → foundations, playground habit, resume audit
60 days → role-typed mocks, cert-prep slice, debug/review drills
90 days → full mocks, story bank, exam or interview date, community
weekly calendar block → practice time that actually exists
on-the-job 90-day plan → cousin: sequenced outcomes after hiring
where_it_breaks: Life happens; slip a week without throwing the camp.
Hiring 90-day plans are job outcomes, not study hours—still sequence them.
This is not a sports product.
90 days will not produce Application Architect from zero—say so.

claims.claim: Trailhead career planning uses discover, plan, and act, and treats planning as ongoing—not a one-time event.
Skill-up plans consider learning (Trailhead), earning (credentials), and connecting (community), plus weekly calendar blocks.
claims.validation: Create a Plan and Skill Up unit.

claims.claim: Get Job Ready groups career planning, resume writing, and interview practice—the job-hunt overlay for a 90-day plan.
claims.validation: Get Job Ready trail and related modules.

claims.claim: Official Admin/Developer/Architect career paths and credential pages are the syllabi; the Admin beginner trail and PD prep trail are concrete 30-day starting points.
claims.validation: Career paths, credential page, foundation trails.

changed_in_release: Interview rewrite 2026-08-16. Exam outlines and trail module lists must be re-checked live before quoting weights or badge names.
unresolved_uncertainty: Whether a given person can pass Platform Administrator in 90 days depends on hours and prior experience—not a platform guarantee.
Application Architect cannot be honestly promised in 90 days from zero; prerequisite lists are Needs verification.

interview_explanation.thirty_seconds: I build thirty-, sixty-, and ninety-day study plans from official career paths and credential pages. 30 foundations, 60 mocks and cert-prep, 90 full interviews or an exam date. No dumps. Weekly hours on a calendar.
interview_explanation.two_minutes: I pick a role. Days 1–30: beginner or PD-fundamentals trail, playground hours, CAREER-009 resume audit. Days 31–60: admin or developer mocks, debug protocol, one official cert-prep module. Days 61–90: Get Job Ready overlay, story bank, community connecting, scheduled exam or interviews. If hours are under three a week, I shrink the earning goal rather than fake a cert. Architect AA is not a 90-day promise from zero.

terminology.precise: Official intro trail, playground cadence, resume inventory, role chosen.

terminology.confusable_neighbor: Onboarding 30-day plan: job cousin, different artifacts.
terminology.boundary: Do not sit a full architect board in week two.

terminology.precise: Role-typed mocks (CAREER-003), debug without guessing, one official cert-prep module.
terminology.example: Weekly admin mock plus Platform Administrator trailmix unit.
terminology.non_example: Collecting 80 unrelated badges with no mock.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Mid-camp injury: slip a week, do not skip mocks forever.

terminology.precise: Full mocks, STAR bank, Get Job Ready, exam or interview date, community connecting.
terminology.example: Scheduled Admin exam in week 12 or three interviews on the calendar.
terminology.non_example: Endless badge collecting with no date.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: On-the-job 90-day plan: outcomes after hire (people, process, org)—still sequenced.
terminology.boundary: Dates can move; plans without dates do not.

terminology.precise: Learn on Trailhead, earn badges/certs, connect in the community.
terminology.example: Earn: sit Admin if ready in days 61–90; connect: one community event in month three.
terminology.non_example: Only lurking with no learning block.
terminology.boundary: Earning a cert you did not study for is not a plan.

terminology.plain: Hours that exist on a real calendar.
terminology.precise: Create-a-plan unit: block weekly development time.
terminology.non_example: Study when I feel like it.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Pomodoro: a technique inside the block.
terminology.boundary: Under three hours/week: shrink the 90-day earning goal.

terminology.plain: Career path + live credential page + named trail.
terminology.precise: Not a blog outline of last year's weights.
terminology.example: Platform Administrator page + admin beginner trail.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Trailmix: official curated set, still not the live exam.

terminology.plain: What you will deliver after you are hired.
terminology.precise: Cousin question: people, process, org outcomes—not only study. Still sequence 30/60/90.
terminology.example: 30: org inventory and user pain; 60: one freeze slice in sandbox; 90: UAT.
terminology.non_example: I will revolutionize the enterprise in week one.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Study 90-day plan: this lesson's default unless they ask on-the-job.
terminology.boundary: Do not promise AA-level architecture in 90 days on the job either.

terminology.plain: Study that never uses unofficial exam items.
terminology.precise: Handbook and Salesforce exam integrity: original practice plus official cert-prep.

when_to_use: When you need thirty-, sixty-, and ninety-day study plans toward a Salesforce admin, developer, or interview date.
When an interviewer asks what you will study or deliver in 90 days and you must sequence outcomes.
When your current habit is random badges or dump PDFs.
When weekly hours are limited and you must shrink the earning goal instead of faking a cert.
When you must put official career-path and credential URLs on the plan.
when_not_to_use: Do not promise Application Architect completion in 90 days from zero.
Do not include unofficial exam dumps in any phase.
Do not skip the first-thirty-day resume audit if you are job hunting.
Do not copy stale exam weights from blogs into the plan.
Do not use a study 90-day plan as a substitute for an on-the-job plan when they asked about the job.

interview_questions.question: How do you build thirty-, sixty-, and ninety-day Salesforce study plans?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Role plus hours. 30 official foundations and playground. 60 role-typed mocks and cert-prep. 90 dates, stories, connecting. No dumps.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I use discover/plan/act and learn/earn/connect. I paste career-path and credential URLs. I calendar-block hours. If hours are low I shrink earning. I will not promise Application Architect from zero. Get Job Ready overlays the job hunt late.
interview_questions.example: Admin, six hours/week, beginner trail then admin mocks then dated exam.
follow_ups: What if I miss a week?

interview_questions.question: How does Trailhead career planning show up on the calendar?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Weekly blocked hours, a written plan, learning plus earning plus connecting—not inspiration-only study.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: Assess Yourself says planning is ongoing. Create-a-plan says block time and review. I put connecting in days 61–90 so it does not vanish. V2MOM wording is optional. The calendar is the artifact.
interview_questions.example: Tue/Thu playground, Saturday mock, monthly plan review.
weak_answer_warnings: Study when I feel like it

interview_questions.question: Give a 90-day admin study plan.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: 30 beginner trail and resume audit. 60 admin mocks, which-tool, debug. 90 Get Job Ready, story bank, dated Admin exam or interviews.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I would name the admin career path and Platform Administrator page. Six hours a week split playground/trail/mock. I refuse dumps. I would not sit the exam in week 3. I would include sharing in every mock.
follow_ups: What if you already know beginner content?

interview_questions.question: Interviewer asks your first 90 days on the job, not your study plan.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: I switch artifacts: org inventory and user pain in 30, one sandbox slice in 60, UAT in 90—not a badge list.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I label the cousin. I still sequence. I do not promise an enterprise rewrite. I ask about their release process. I keep study habits as a side line, not the job plan. Sharing and a freeze slice beat 40 badges.
interview_questions.example: 30: who owns what in the org. 60: legal-freeze sandbox. 90: UAT with sales ops.
weak_answer_warnings: I will transform everything in week one

interview_questions.question: You badge-collected for 60 days and fail mocks. Fix the remaining 30.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Stop unrelated badges. Run role-typed mocks, debug protocol, and story bank until the date.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: Phase 60 was skipped in spirit. I put CAREER-003 and CAREER-004 on the calendar now. I shrink earning if the exam was the only date. I do not add dumps to catch up. I review the plan as Assess Yourself says.
interview_questions.example: Eight remaining Saturdays: four admin mocks, two debug labs, two STAR rehearsals.

interview_questions.question: Hours dropped to two per week. Recover the plan.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: I shrink the 90-day earning goal, keep playground plus one mock type, and move the exam.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: Create-a-plan requires hours that exist. I will not keep a fake Admin-in-90 promise. Connecting might become one asynchronous community post. Foundations continue so the camp does not die. I rewrite the one-pager.
interview_questions.example: New 90-day goal: finish beginner trail and four mocks; exam next quarter.

interview_questions.question: Design a dump-free 60-day cert-prep slice for PD.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Official Prepare-for-development trail units on fundamentals, automation, UI, testing/debug—plus original Apex/LWC mocks.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I open the live PD credential page for orientation, not for leaked items. I schedule the testing/debug cert-prep module beside CAREER-004 labs. I write original scenarios. I refuse friend PDFs. Earning the exam sits in days 61–90 only if mocks show readiness—Needs verification personally.
interview_questions.example: Saturday: cert-prep unit. Sunday: original bulk+test mock.
tradeoffs: Coverage of exam sections vs mock skills

interview_questions.question: Teach 30/60/90 with the training-camp analogy and where it breaks.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Conditioning, scrimmages, game weeks. It breaks when life slips a week or when someone promises a championship (AA) in one camp.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: 30 is conditioning on official trails, 60 is scrimmages (mocks), 90 is games (exam/interviews). Playbooks are credential pages. Dumps are stolen sheets. It breaks because hiring 90-day plans are job outcomes, because hours vary, and because Salesforce is not a sport. I then give an admin six-hour-week camp with URLs.
interview_questions.example: Beginner trail; admin mocks; Get Job Ready plus a date; refuse dumps.
weak_answer_warnings: AA championship in 90 days from zero
